summary: Adds three endpoints to the directory API: a user search by name, a per-key request counter guarded by a mutex, and an upstream status probe.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf. A quote in name breaks out of the string literal.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can run arbitrary SQL against the database. That caller can read or change every table.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter. Keep the SQL text constant.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count takes h.mu before it checks the key. The empty-key branch returns without unlocking h.mu.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key leaves h.mu locked forever. Every later Count request then blocks, and its goroutine leaks.
findings.fix: Check the key before taking the lock. Alternatively, unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close() before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil and the deferred call dereferences nil.
findings.consequence: Each request to GET /upstream panics while the upstream is unreachable. The client gets a dropped connection instead of the intended 502.
findings.fix: Move the defer below the error check.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds Search, Count, Upstream and fetchStatus. The repository has no test file that exercises them.
findings.consequence: Tests would have caught the lock leak and the nil body panic. Future changes to these handlers can regress without notice.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each handler. Include the empty-key and unreachable-upstream paths.

dropped.reason: This reports the same formatted query as c1. The finding for c1 already covers it.
